identity.gender_note: In Arabic and Muslim naming Ali is a male name; in English it is also a short form of female names such as Alison or Alexandra, which is a separate name.

core_meaning.primary_meaning: Ali (Arabic عَلِيّ, ʿAlī) is an Arabic male given name meaning “high” or “elevated”, from the root ʕ-l-w. In Muslim naming it honours Ali ibn Abi Talib, cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad and the fourth Caliph of Sunni Islam.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The name comes from the Arabic triconsonantal root ʕ-l-w, whose core sense is height — “high”, “elevated”, and by extension “champion” or “sublime”. It was already in use among some pre-Islamic Arabs, and it is identical in form and meaning to Hebrew Eli (עֵלִי), the name of the High Priest in the Books of Samuel.

etymology.morphology: Adjective of the faʿīl pattern on the root ʿ-l-w, “to be high”.
etymology.etymology_explanation: From the Arabic triconsonantal root ʕ-l-w, which literally means “high” or “elevated”; cognate with Hebrew Eli.
etymology.false_etymology_warning: English “Ali” as a short form of Alison, Alice or Alexandra is a different name with a different origin.

origin.origin_explanation: Arabic; present among some pre-Islamic Arabs and spread across the Muslim world through veneration of Ali ibn Abi Talib. As a surname it is the most common last name in several Gulf and Horn of Africa countries.

religion.primary_association: Islamic — name of Ali ibn Abi Talib
religion.religious_status: Name of the fourth Caliph and first Shia Imam
religion.religious_explanation: Ali ibn Abi Talib (601–661) was the cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad, the fourth Caliph of Sunni Islam and, in Shia Islam, the first Imam. Several later Shia Imams also bore the name, such as Ali ibn Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) and Ali al-Ridha.

companion_status.reference: Ali ibn Abi Talib (601–661), cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet

cultural_context.cultural_meaning: Among Shia Muslims especially, the name carries deep devotion to Ali and the Imams who followed him.
cultural_context.impact: Ali is the most common last name in Qatar, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates, Somalia, Kuwait and Libya.

pronunciation.note: Arabic begins with the throat consonant ʿayn (ع), which English lacks; the stress falls on the long final -ī. Urdu and Persian speakers say AH-lee.

name_variants.variant_notes: Aly is a common Egyptian spelling. Hebrew Eli shares the same form and meaning.

known_linguistic_history: Recorded among pre-Islamic Arabs, including the Banu Hanifa and rulers of Saba and Himyar.
Became one of the central Muslim names through Ali ibn Abi Talib (601–661) and the Shia Imams named after him.
historical_context.historical_person_association: Ali ibn Abi Talib (601–661), fourth Caliph of Sunni Islam and first Shia Imam.

modern_usage.modern_context: Common as both a given name and a surname throughout the Muslim world and among Indian and Pakistani Muslims.

faq.q: Is Ali related to the Hebrew name Eli?
faq.a: They are identical in form and meaning: Hebrew Eli (עֵלִי), the High Priest in the Books of Samuel, also means “high”.

faq.q: Is Ali a boy or girl name?
faq.a: In Arabic and Muslim naming it is a boy's name. In English, Ali can also be a nickname for Alison or Alexandra, which is a different name.
AH-lee in English; Arabic /ʕaˈliː/ begins with the ʿayn sound and stresses the long final vowel.

islamic_naming_context.context: One of the most widely used names among both Sunni and Shia Muslims; frequently combined, e.g. Muhammad Ali, Ali Reza, Ali Akbar.
islamic_naming_context.interpretation: Chosen for its sense of height and nobility and for Ali ibn Abi Talib.
islamic_naming_context.important_distinction: Al-ʿAlī (“the Most High”) is one of the names of God; as a personal name it is used without the article.

numerology.meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ali total 4, associated with stability, discipline and order. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.
